title: Sleeping in on Weekends May Be Bad for Your Heart
paragraphs: Many people stay up late on Friday night and then sleep in on the weekend. It might feel good, but a new study suggests that changing your sleep schedule like this may be bad for your heart.

The study was presented at a meeting of the American Heart Association in November 2026. It was led by Nguyen Minh Tuan Viet of Harvard Medical School. The researchers used information from more than 10,300 adults in the United States. These people wore Fitbit devices for six months. The devices recorded when people went to bed, when they woke up and how they slept. In total, the researchers studied more than one million hours of sleep.

The researchers found that people whose sleep schedules changed a lot had about a 20% higher risk of serious heart problems, such as heart attacks, strokes and heart failure. In addition, every 29-minute change in how long people slept was linked to a 24% higher risk of these problems. This was true whether people slept more or less than usual.
According to Viet, much of this change in sleep happens on weekends, when people go to bed later on Friday night. Shift work can also cause it.
Viet says people should try to keep a regular sleep schedule. This means going to bed and waking up at the same times every day, and sleeping for about the same amount of time each night.
However, the study is still at an early stage. It also only shows a link between irregular sleep and heart problems. It does not prove that changing sleep schedules causes heart problems.
